hero.tagline: Engineering Reliable Traffic Systems — and Applying AI to Smarter Mobility
hero.description:
Senior Service Engineer with 10+ years of multidisciplinary engineering experience, including 6+ years supporting intelligent transportation, smart infrastructure, and traffic enforcement systems across the UAE.

I integrate cameras, LiDAR, sensors, control units, networks, databases, and backend platforms into reliable end-to-end operational systems.
currentFocus: Reliable ITS integration and operational performance
Data quality, model efficiency, and explainable AI

about.heading: Engineering at the Intersection of ITS, Systems Integration, and Applied AI
paragraphs: I am a Senior Service Engineer specializing in intelligent transportation systems, smart infrastructure, and traffic enforcement.

My background spans electronics, embedded systems, network infrastructure, software automation, and the integration of complex operational systems. Over the past 6+ years, I have supported ITS deployments across the UAE, working across cameras, LiDAR, sensors, control units, networking, databases, and backend platforms.

My work covers FAT and SAT, commissioning, calibration, interface validation, performance verification, technical documentation, incident support, and structured root-cause analysis across hardware, software, communication, and database layers.
I work closely with customers, vendors, software teams, and field engineers to resolve complex integration issues and support reliable service delivery.

Alongside my engineering role, I am pursuing an MSc in Artificial Intelligence at UWE Bristol. My current academic work applies machine learning and computer vision to transportation problems, with a particular focus on data quality, leakage-resistant evaluation, efficient neural networks, and model explainability.
My long-term direction is to combine real-world ITS engineering with applied computer vision to build safer, more reliable, and more intelligent mobility infrastructure.

projects.category: MSc Artificial Intelligence Research · Computer Vision · PyTorch
projects.title: Efficient Neural Network Architectures for Vehicle Type Classification
projects.subtitle: A content-audited, leakage-aware, and efficiency-focused study using VTID2
projects.description: Developed and evaluated neural network architectures for vehicle type classification using the VTID2 image dataset. The evaluated architectures included an MLP, a standard CNN, an efficient depthwise-separable CNN, and an efficient CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation.

meta.label: Author
meta.value: Mohammed Mahyoub

meta.label: Problem
meta.value: A content-based dataset audit identified 2,425 redundant exact copies among 4,356 valid images, leaving 1,931 exact-unique images.

meta.label: Method
meta.value: Compared conventional and leakage-controlled evaluation protocols, and examined the trade-off between classification performance and computational efficiency.

meta.label: Result
meta.value: The efficient CNN achieved substantial reductions in trainable parameters and MACs while maintaining competitive Macro-F1. Grad-CAM was used to analyse model attention and the influence of preprocessing and letterbox padding.

status.label: Academic Research — Code Private During Assessment

projects.imageAlt: Conceptual illustration of three stylized vehicle silhouettes (car, truck, motorcycle) feeding into a glowing compact neural network with layered nodes and a visual attention heatmap

projects.title: Vehicle Type Classification Using NGSIM US-101
projects.description: Developed and evaluated supervised machine-learning models for classifying motorcycles, passenger cars, and trucks using the NGSIM US-101 traffic trajectory dataset. Models compared: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest.

meta.label: Author
meta.value: Mohammed Mahyoub

meta.label: Method
meta.value: Vehicle records were aggregated to the vehicle level to reduce data leakage and create independent observations for training and evaluation.

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: Data preprocessing, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model comparison, hyperparameter optimisation, classification evaluation, and feature-importance analysis.

projects.title: Autonomous Quadcopter UAV — Flight Control, Telemetry & FPV
projects.subtitle: ArduPilot APM 2.6 quadcopter built, tuned and flight-tested across autonomous modes
projects.description: Designed, assembled and flight-tested an autonomous quadcopter with GPS waypoint navigation, MAVLink telemetry to a ground control station, failsafe protection, and a live 5.8 GHz video link for remote surveillance.

meta.label: Author
meta.value: Mohammed Mahyoub

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: Team project covering propulsion sizing, airframe and electronics integration, sensor calibration, PID tuning, flight-mode and failsafe testing, telemetry and video systems, and technical documentation.

meta.label: Build
meta.value: DJI F450 frame, 4× DJI 2212/920KV motors with 30A ESCs, 3S LiPo, APM 2.6 (MPU6000 IMU, barometer), uBlox NEO-6M GPS/compass, sonar and optical-flow sensors, 3DR 433 MHz telemetry (≈400 m range tested), 2.4 GHz RC via PPM encoder, 5.8 GHz video with MinimOSD. Propulsion sized in eCalc (≈1.6 kg all-up weight).

meta.label: Testing
meta.value: Calibrated accelerometer, compass, RC and ESCs; tuned the PIDs (final rate gains roll/pitch P 0.15 · I 0.10 · D 0.004, stabilize P 4.5); flight-tested Stabilize, Loiter, AltHold, Auto (waypoints), Guided and Follow-Me (phone GCS), plus radio, geofence and battery failsafes (land / return-to-launch).

meta.label: Fixes
meta.value: Root-caused faults from flight logs: re-centred an off-centre IMU causing drift; damped vibration and shielded the barometer for Loiter; low-pass filtered sonar for AltHold; moved the compass away from ≈80% motor interference and set local magnetic declination (2.11°E) to correct Auto-mode heading.

meta.label: Study
meta.value: Backed by a UAS communications study: command-and-control and telemetry links (GSM/GPRS, line-of-sight 900 MHz–5.8 GHz) and UAS spectrum requirements (ITU-R M.2171).

projects.title: Software-Defined Networking — Automation & Video Streaming
projects.description: Implemented an OpenDaylight/OpenFlow network with Mininet and real IP network integration, using controller APIs to automate forwarding and evaluate video streaming. A separate Ryu/Open vSwitch extension provides reproducible measurements.

meta.label: Original
meta.value: OpenDaylight, Postman, XML forwarding rules, Python topologies, connectivity restoration and video streaming across Mininet and a real IP network.

meta.label: Author
meta.value: Mohammed Mahyoub

meta.label: Role
meta.value: End-to-end design, implementation, programming, testing and technical documentation.

meta.label: Automation
meta.value: Reproducible Ryu extension: Python REST client (and Postman collection) for the Ryu ofctl_rest API. Flow tables for three switches are computed from the topology and installed in 21 REST calls (0.038 s); after the s3 table is wiped, h4→h6 connectivity is restored in 7 calls (0.008 s).

meta.label: Streaming
meta.value: Reproducible Ryu extension: 2.5 Mbit/s H.264 stream from h1 to h6 across the three-switch path, rate-limited with OpenFlow 1.3 meters at 3000, 1500 and 800 kbit/s; quality measured with FFmpeg PSNR/SSIM.

meta.label: Ryu results
meta.value: Reproducible Ryu extension: No meter / 3000 kbit/s: PSNR ≈ 40 dB, SSIM 0.998. 1500 kbit/s: 19.3 dB, SSIM 0.819. 800 kbit/s: 15.4 dB, SSIM 0.706. All logs, flow dumps and raw results are in the repository.

links.label: View GitHub Repository — code, results & figures

projects.category: Telecommunications · IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) · VoIP / IPTV / VoLTE
projects.title: IMS Multimedia Services — VoIP, IPTV & VoLTE
projects.subtitle: Cisco CUCM/CME voice network on GNS3, VLC IPTV, VoLTE over LTE/IMS in OPNET, plus a reproducible Kamailio + Asterisk IMS lab with measured QoS
projects.description: Independent project on IP multimedia services around an IMS core: VoIP on Cisco Unified Communications (CUCM 8.6 and a three-router GNS3 network with a branch CME), IPTV streaming over the LAN with VLC, and VoLTE simulated in OPNET Modeler with an IMS core connected to the PSTN, plus an IMS case study for a fixed-line and a mobile operator. The same service areas were then rebuilt as a reproducible open-source lab with measured results.

meta.label: Author
meta.value: Mohammed Mahyoub

meta.label: Role
meta.value: Team design, implementation and testing of the project; design, implementation and testing of the reproducible lab.

meta.label: VoIP (Cisco)
meta.value: CUCM 8.6 on VMware; HQ voice gateway (H.323 to CUCM), branch router with Cisco Unified CME for survivability, and a PSTN router in GNS3. VoIP dial-peers, G.711 codec class, H.323↔SIP interworking, TFTP provisioning and Extension Mobility; SCCP and SIP endpoints including Android.

meta.label: IPTV
meta.value: VLC streaming over HTTP and UDP with optional transcoding, watched on laptops and mobile phones.

meta.label: VoLTE (OPNET)
meta.value: LTE-like access built from the 802.16e model (4 cells, OFDMA 20 MHz, 2×1 MIMO, Gold UGS voice class) with a P/I/S-CSCF + HSS core and PSTN interworking; voice traffic, handovers, jitter, delay and throughput measured.

meta.label: Case study
meta.value: Three IMS adoption paths for a fixed-line (PTC) and a mobile operator (Yemen Mobile): NGN upgrade, converged core (HSS/SLF, SBC, PCRF options) and two new IMS cores.

meta.label: Reproducible lab
meta.value: Kamailio P-CSCF/S-CSCF + Asterisk AS with digest registration and iFC service routing; G.711 over a congested 10 Mbit/s trunk: FIFO MOS 1.83 vs EF/CS3 priority MOS 4.27; IPTV multicast with IGMP snooping halves trunk traffic for two viewers.

projects.title: Software-Defined Data Center (SDDC) — Design & Implementation
projects.subtitle: Compute, storage and network virtualisation hosting directory, cloud-application, web and e-mail services
projects.description: Designed and implemented a working software-defined data center on physical hardware, virtualising compute, storage and networking and hosting directory, cloud-application, web and e-mail services.

meta.label: Author
meta.value: Mohammed Mahyoub

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: Team project covering design, implementation, configuration, testing and technical documentation, alongside a study of SDDC architecture, storage networking (DAS/NAS/SAN, FC, IP SAN), network virtualisation and cloud models.

meta.label: Storage
meta.value: FreeNAS 11 on a dedicated server: ZFS volumes exported over iSCSI (portal, authorised initiators, CHAP authentication, target–extent LUN mapping) and attached to ESXi as shared storage.

meta.label: Compute
meta.value: VMware ESXi 5.5 on an Intel Core i7 host (20 GB RAM) managed with vSphere Client, running Windows Server 2008 R2 virtual machines with planned CPU, memory and thick/thin disk provisioning; storage served by an AMD Opteron server with SAS and SATA disks.

meta.label: Network
meta.value: ESXi standard vSwitch with network labels and optional VLAN IDs, plus NIC teaming (active/standby), on a switched LAN with Wi-Fi access.

meta.label: Services
meta.value: AD/DNS/DHCP domain controller; Citrix XenApp 6.5 farm publishing applications to domain users via Citrix Receiver; AppServ web stack (Apache, PHP, MySQL); Exchange 2013 with OWA/ECP, PowerShell mailbox provisioning, groups, connectors and transport rules.

projects.title: RFID Library Automation System (ISO 15693)
projects.description: Implemented a radio-frequency identification (RFID) system for library automation: tagged items are identified over RF by readers at the counter, self-service kiosk, shelves and exit gates, with every transaction recorded in a host database.

meta.label: Role
meta.value: Design, implementation and technical presentation of the system.

meta.label: How it works
meta.value: The reader energizes the tag through its antenna (RF coupling); the tag returns its data, which the host PC logs in the database and can write back to the tag. A personalizer programs tags for new items.

meta.label: Tags
meta.value: Chip, antenna and package. Passive HF tags (reader-powered, centimetres at the pad up to about 1 m at the gates, about USD 1, no maintenance) chosen over active tags (battery, up to 100 m, up to 128 KB, USD 10–100).

meta.label: Reader
meta.value: ISO 15693 at 13.56 MHz, RS-232 interface, SIP / STX-ETX protocol, metal housing, 230 V, CE and radio approval.

meta.label: Library use
meta.value: Staff counter, self check-in/out kiosk, handheld shelf inventory, book-drop and security gates: faster circulation, fast inventory, theft prevention and usage statistics.

projects.title: Line-of-Sight & Fresnel Zone Wireless Planning Tool
projects.description: Developed a planning tool for line-of-sight analysis and Fresnel-zone clearance in point-to-point wireless links.

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: Line-of-sight establishes the direct path between antennas. Fresnel analysis examines clearance around that path, giving the planner a different view from a power-only link budget.

projects.title: Wireless Coverage & Point-to-Point Network Planning
projects.description: Modelled wireless coverage and point-to-point connectivity, considering antenna alignment, capacity requirements and site coverage.

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: Coverage describes where access is available; point-to-point planning describes the transport between sites. Antenna placement and alignment influence both the proposed link and its installation.

projects.title: Network Infrastructure Design — MPLS Backbone
projects.description: Built and validated a Cisco 7200 MPLS backbone in GNS3, using OSPF, MPLS traffic engineering, VRF/MPLS VPN and MP-BGP for multi-site connectivity.

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: OSPF provides the routing underlay. MPLS carries labelled traffic, while VRFs separate customer routing contexts and MP-BGP exchanges VPN routes.
